question:
A fractional function is defined with carefully chosen domain and codomain. Let $A=\mathbb{R}-\{3\}$ and $B=\mathbb{R}-\{1\}$, and define $f:A\to B$ by $f(x)=\frac{x-2}{x-3}$. The value $x=3$ is excluded because the denominator would be zero, while the codomain excludes $1$. Students must examine whether the restrictions make the function one-one and onto. In particular, they compare two arbitrary inputs for injectivity and solve the equation $f(x)=y$ for an arbitrary $y\in B$ to investigate surjectivity.

(a) Calculate $f(2)$ and $f(4)$.

(b) Show that $f(x)$ can never equal $1$ for any $x\in A$.

(c) Prove that $f$ is one-one.

(d) For arbitrary $y\in B$, solve $f(x)=y$ and use the result to determine whether $f$ is onto.
explanation:
(a)
$f(2)= rac{2-2}{2-3}=0$ and $f(4)= rac{4-2}{4-3}=2$.

(b)
If $f(x)=1$, then $ rac{x-2}{x-3}=1$. Since $x eq3$, multiplying by $x-3$ gives $x-2=x-3$, which implies $-2=-3$, an impossibility. Therefore, $f(x) eq1$ for every $x\in A$, so the stated codomain $B=\mathbb{R}-\{1\}$ is appropriate.

(c)
Suppose $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$. Then $ rac{x_1-2}{x_1-3}= rac{x_2-2}{x_2-3}$. Cross-multiplying gives $(x_1-2)(x_2-3)=(x_2-2)(x_1-3)$. Expanding and simplifying gives $x_1=x_2$. Hence, $f$ is one-one.

(d)
Let $y\in B$. Then $y eq1$. Solving $ rac{x-2}{x-3}=y$ gives $x-2=yx-3y$, so $x(1-y)=2-3y$. Hence $x= rac{2-3y}{1-y}$. Since $y eq1$, this value is defined. Also, it cannot equal $3$, because $ rac{2-3y}{1-y}=3$ would give $2=3$, which is impossible. Thus $x\in A$ and $f(x)=y$. Therefore, every $y\in B$ has a pre-image, so $f$ is onto.

options.A: $f(2)=0$ and $f(4)=2$; $f(x)\neq1$ for every $x\in A$, $f$ is one-one, and every $y\in B$ has the pre-image $x=\frac{2-3y}{1-y}$. Hence, $f$ is onto.
options.B: $f(2)=0$ and $f(4)=2$; $f(x)$ can equal $1$, and $f$ is onto but not one-one because two distinct inputs may have the same image.
options.C: $f(2)=2$ and $f(4)=0$; $f$ is one-one but not onto because every $y\in B$ would require the pre-image $x=\frac{2-y}{3-y}$.
options.D: $f(2)=0$ and $f(4)=2$; $f(x)\neq1$, but $f$ is neither one-one nor onto because the excluded value $x=3$ has no image.
